_meta.description: Everything that must be answered before a decision can reasonably be made, separated into what the repository already knows, what it does not know, and how the missing piece could be discovered. Each gap names the owner who can actually answer it, because most of these are not research problems: they are facts only the account holder, a seller, or a lawyer can supply.

kinds.Known: Answered from an official source that was read, with the source linked. Listed so a reviewer does not have to re-derive it.
kinds.Unknown - discoverable: Not known yet, but an official source or a reachable party can supply it. The row says exactly where to look.
kinds.Unknown - not discoverable from here: No public official source exists for it in this environment. It needs an account, a legal opinion or a seller. Listed so nobody spends another session looking for it.
kinds.Owner decision: Not a fact at all. A choice only the site owner can make; the row lists the options and what each one commits the site to.

_meta.rule: An Unknown is never closed by inference. It is closed by a named source, a named party's answer, or an explicit owner decision recorded in the Decision log.

questions.question: Is the Associates account enrolled under the supplied Partner Tag, and have the published links been generated and validated in that account?
questions.why_it_matters: Without an account there is no tag, and without a tag no click can be attributed. Every revenue figure the brief asks for is downstream of this single fact.
questions.known: The user supplied `shopnow047c-20` as the selected tracking ID. This session cannot confirm that it is active, belongs to an enrolled Associates account, or has been applied to any Special Link. The three previously reviewed destinations had no visible `tag=` parameter in their 2026-11-16 re-check. The two additional URLs are separately unverified (F-55); their destinations were later resolved to meat thermometers and held (F-56). The 2026-11-17 reads (data/verification-session-1f4a7a22.json) re-resolved the three links to the same ASINs, again with no tag=; decisions D-01/D-14 (recorded 2026-11-17) publish the tagged Special Links (https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=shopnow047c-20) as the outbound hrefs, while the supplied short links stay recorded, unjudged (FLG-003 unresolved). Whether the ID is registered and active is question Q-50.
questions.how_to_discover: In Associates Central, confirm account enrollment and that shopnow047c-20 is the account Partner Tag. Generate or validate one Special Link per intended product; re-resolve each destination and confirm a test click in the authorized reporting workflow before scaling.
questions.answerable_by: The site owner

sources.ref: Operating Agreement (the agreement that creates the account and the tag)

questions.known: Amazon's own Creators API introduction states the prerequisite. The site currently publishes no price or rating (F-02).

questions.known: Both clauses are quoted verbatim in the repository and in flag F-12 and finding A-08. The narrower reading, that the clauses restrict training on Amazon content rather than the writing of original copy, is recorded there with its sources.
questions.how_to_discover: Counsel reads the cited clauses. Nothing on the public web resolves it, and no further reading of the same pages will change the answer.

questions.question: What counts as success, and over what period?
questions.why_it_matters: The brief asks for click and conversion tracking, but a new site with no traffic will show zeros for months. questions.how_to_discover: Host the endpoint (D-43, owner-side), then read daily guide_read_75 counts per path after 14 days. Compare the rate per guide, not the raw count, so a longer guide is not punished for its length.
questions.answerable_by: The site owner, once the endpoint is hosted (D-43). The agent can read the counts the moment they exist.
